title: SAML 2.0 dry-run connector: simulated assertion replay + metadata delta reconciler
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Build a SAML 2.0 'dry-run' onboarding flow that allows admins to: (1) upload or fetch IdP metadata, (2) run a simulated assertion replay against current metadata and existing user mappings, (3) surface metadata deltas with an automated reconciler that suggests authoritative values and safe fixes, and (4) preview the exact changes and audit log entries before committing. This ticket scopes backend validation logic, reconciliation heuristics, admin preview UI hooks, RBAC v2 gating for approvals, and audit-log instrumentation. Goal: reduce failed connector rollouts and manual troubleshooting while preserving security and operator control.
acceptance_criteria: Dry-run mode can be triggered from connector setup and will not modify live connector config
Simulated assertion replay generates deterministic success/failure reports using sample assertions provided by admin
Metadata delta reconciler produces a ranked list of suggested fixes (certificate rotation, endpoint URL normalization, attribute mapping hints) with confidence scores
Admin preview UI receives a compact patch summary and can accept, reject, or partially apply suggestions
All actions (dry-run, reconcile suggestions, accept/reject) emit audit log events compatible with the console audit schema
RBAC v2 prevents non-admin roles from applying reconciler fixes; enforcement tested via unit + integration tests
End-to-end test coverage: 90% for critical validation paths; performance under typical connector creation workload <150ms validation latency for metadata fetch + local parsing
implementation_steps: Design API: /connectors/:id/dry-run POST with metadata source and optional sample-assertions payload
Backend: metadata parser + validation pipeline (schema checks, cert parsing, endpoint probe, fingerprint diff)
Simulated assertion runner: replay provided SAML assertions against current ACS and mapping logic to report mapping failures
Delta reconciler: rule engine to match common fixes and compute confidence scores; produce patch set
Audit logging: augment audit entries for dry-run and apply events (who, when, diff, confidence)
RBAC: wire console permissions to new apply-suggested-fix action and add unit tests
UI: admin preview modal with suggested diffs, inline explanations, and one-click apply (subject to RBAC)
Integration tests: connector onboarding scenario (happy path, cert mismatch, attribute-mapping failure, expired cert), and load test for parallel dry-runs
Security review and threat modeling for automated patch suggestions to prevent unsafe overwrites
risk_and_mitigation: Automated reconciler may propose unsafe changes (e.g., swap endpoints) — mitigation: require explicit admin approval and RBAC gating
Certificate handling must not expose private keys — mitigation: only parse public certs from metadata; never accept private key material
False positives in simulated assertion replay — mitigation: include sample-assertions upload and show raw vs. mapped claim diff so admins can inspect
Performance regression in metadata ingestion — mitigation: cache validated metadata bundles and rate-limit remote metadata fetches
security_considerations: All metadata fetches use TLS with strict cert validation and HSTS; follow redirect policy and timeouts
Audit logs must contain enough context for compliance (operator id, connector id, delta summary) and be redact-safe for PII
Automated suggestions must be recorded as suggestions (not auto-applied) unless explicitly enabled by customer with appropriate policy
RBAC v2 integration required to ensure only privileged roles can commit reconciler patches
testing_notes: Unit tests: metadata parsing edge cases (multiple certs, missing entityID, xml namespace variants)
Integration tests: run simulated assertions using test IdPs (SSOCorp sandbox) and verify mapping to internal user objects
E2E QA: run a canary group of existing customers with opt-in dry-run telemetry to surface real-world metadata shapes
Load test: 200 concurrent dry-run requests to validate rate limits and backend scaling
